rulings.challenge_claim: unit_type 'dialogue_exchange' is applied to an atomized single-voice question that contains no alternation, contrary to the category's own definition, and no deviation disclosure is given.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. MT 5:9 = WEB 5:9 (crosswalk-checked, outside the offset zone) is one uninterrupted chorus turn: the doubled interrogative מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) occurs twice in-verse and the two runs are byte-identical (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse), and the verse carries no second turn - the answering wasf is a separate row at web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16. In the closed vocabulary dialogue_exchange is rapid attributed alternation held as ONE unit; a single turn does not carry that form, and the operative-category law that permits any vocabulary value the row's own bytes carry also requires a one-sentence deviation disclosure, which the device note (intra-verse doubling only) does not supply. Tier-1 bounding markers do exist on both edges under the moderate voice policy - the 2fs suffix on דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) fixing a female addressee against the 1cs voice of the preceding narrative, and her own answering opener דּוֹדִ֥י (oshb:Song.5.10, byte tier) - which is the lyric_address pattern, not the dialogue_exchange one.
rulings.remedy: Re-label unit_type to lyric_address and cite the two tier-1 bounding markers as spliced, tier-labelled forms (the 2fs addressee suffix at oshb:Song.5.9; the answering opener at oshb:Song.5.10); or keep dialogue_exchange and add the mandated one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field and must be re-cut with whichever label survives. Cure test (the test that killed the original): a reviewer reading only the row's own span bytes must find the form the unit_type names - MT 5:9 alone must exhibit alternation if dialogue_exchange is kept. A third cure, widening the span to web:Song.5.9-Song.5.16, is a boundary PROPOSAL only (explicit boss adoption required) and collides with the web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16 wasf bound that both primaries supported.

rulings.challenge_claim: The chorus attribution is built on an addressee marker only, dropping the verse's plural-speaker form and the quoted-back oath that straddles the front seam; the attribution 'lands exactly on' the tier-4 WEB voice heading; and the device note contradicts a byte-tier cross-verse recurrence.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT from the LF item on this row, not the same defect: LF challenges the unit_type, OL challenges the evidence base. Two sub-claims verified, two mis-framed. VERIFIED: הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) carries the 1cp object suffix and is the only in-verse form that makes the speakers plural; it is uncited, so the PLURAL chorus identification is under-evidenced. VERIFIED: the oath root straddles the row's own front seam - הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי (oshb:Song.5.8, byte tier) against הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier), skeleton sweep: 5 verses (MT 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 5:9, 8:4), the root being oath-only in this book with the speech roles split (adjuration at 5:8; the daughters quoting it back at 5:9) - and the rationale gives a forward reason for the cut only, so the cross-seam cohesion rule is unmet. REFINED (1): that a 2fs suffix 'cannot carry a daughters-attribution' overstates the moderate policy - a 2fs addressee marker set against the 1cs voice of the preceding narrative IS a tier-1 warrant for a shift AWAY from her voice; what it cannot carry is the plural identity. And 'lands exactly on the tier-4 heading' is a provenance inference, not a byte finding: the heading catalog audits a claim AGAINST heading-leaning, it cannot establish that a row leaned on one, and tier-4 is never evidence in either direction. REFINED (2): the charge that the device note contradicts a recurrence claim is an object error - the note's disclaimer object is מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 in-verse, byte-identical), which is genuinely intra-verse-only. The real gap is a different object: the row quotes הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Song.5.9) inside its own run, and that IS a byte-tier cross-verse recurrence (byte sweep: 3 verses - MT 1:8, 5:9, 6:1), untier-labelled and undisclosed.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale, splice and tier-label הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) as the plural-speaker evidence, keeping the 2fs addressee marker as the shift-away-from-her warrant it actually is. Add a cross-seam disclosure sentence for the oath root shared with oshb:Song.5.8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses; oath-only root, speech role named on each side), and add web:Song.5.8 to boundary_evidence_refs so the mirror holds. Tier-label the הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים vocative as a byte-tier recurrence (byte sweep: 3 verses) or drop the quoted run. Add nothing about the WEB voice heading in either direction. Cure test: every voice-IDENTITY word in the row must trace to an in-verse form that marks the SPEAKER, not the addressee, and every cross-verse recurrence sentence must name its object and its tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The daughters-attribution again rests on an addressee marker rather than the verse's plural-speaker forms; the mutual-belonging shape discipline is performed entirely in transliteration with neither rival spliced, one of them located by position instead of a coordinate inside the offset zone; and the closing-clause bond with the named rival is undisclosed and mis-weighted at tier.
rulings.grounds: Three sub-claims verified, one mis-framed. VERIFIED: the cited דּוֹדֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) marks only the addressee, while וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ (1cp) and עִמָּֽךְ (2fs) in the same verse (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) - the forms that actually make the speakers plural - go uncited; the same under-evidencing class as the MT 5:9 row, so this is a cluster-level pattern, not an isolated slip. VERIFIED: neither rival shape is spliced, against the engagement-class rule that pointed splices plus tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; the attested rivals are דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, byte tier) and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier). VERIFIED and tier-corrected: the row's close הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.6.3) and the rival's close הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.2.16) are identical at SKELETON tier only (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; byte sweep: 1 verse each - they split on the shin dagesh), so this is a closer cross-verse bond than the word-order contrast the note actually draws, and any byte-identity claim there would be false. REFINED on framing: OL calls the missing coordinate an offset-zone disclosure failure, but the offset-zone rule binds STRUCTURED refs and the device note writes no ref at all, so no offset-zone violation occurs there. The actual violation is the register purge - 'held later in this part' is a positional/part reference where cross-row references must be verse-anchored. Also refined: the remark that a high confidence band 'sits oddly' here is taste, not defect - the row's close does rest on a tier-1 formula anchor that survives the bytes, and the confidence band is not challenged by this ruling.
rulings.remedy: Splice both rival shapes into device_notes with tier labels and verse-anchored coordinates - דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, byte tier) and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier; the dual is mandatory there) - replacing 'held later in this part' entirely. Add the shared closing clause as a skeleton-tier bond (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; byte sweep: 1 verse each, splitting on the shin dagesh) rather than leaving the word-order contrast as the only stated relation. In boundary_rationale, cite וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ and עִמָּֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) as the plural-speaker evidence. Cure tests: no positional or part reference survives in any field; every offset-zone coordinate written anywhere on the row carries a dual; and every recurrence sentence names its tier, with no byte-identity wording on the shin-dagesh pair.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF and OL raise the SAME defect: the row's load-bearing claim that no tier-1 voice-shift marker separates 6:5-7 from 6:8-9 is byte-false, since the 2fs address forms stop at MT 6:7 and MT 6:8-6:9 carry none.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently and sustained. Word-final-kaf 2fs surface audit over the span (pointed bytes; no morphology layer is staged, so this is reported at surface grade - the same grade the row's own gender claims stand on): MT 6:4 = 0, MT 6:5 = 2, MT 6:6 = 1, MT 6:7 = 2 (the verse closing on לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ, oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier), MT 6:8 = 0, MT 6:9 = 0. MT 6:9 instead predicates הִיא֙ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) three times with the 3fs mappiq suffixes לְאִמָּ֔הּ and לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier); its יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) are 1cs-POSSESSIVE epithets, not address forms. So the row's 'the same male address-voice governs the whole span' is true of MT 6:4-6:7 only, and an in-verse morphological marker of exactly the tier-1 class does sit at the 6:7|6:8 join the row declines to cut; the marker is denied rather than engaged, and the universals check independently flags the sentence as a digit-less universal. LF and OL are the SAME defect, not two. Object correction to LF's supporting gloss: MT 6:7 closes on לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ 'your veil/locks', not on רַקָּתֵ֔ךְ 'your temple', which is mid-verse - the finding survives the correction, but the challenge named the wrong count-object for its closing token. LF's added observation is sound: an enallage reading (person shift without speaker shift, as registered for the 1:2-4 zone) is available to keep the wider bound, but the row never makes it.
rulings.remedy: Replace the absence claim in boundary_rationale AND in strongest_rejected_alternative with the audited person-form facts (2fs address forms present MT 6:5-6:7, absent MT 6:8-6:9; MT 6:9 3fs predication with 1cs-possessive epithets, spliced and tier-labelled), and argue the wider bound POSITIVELY - either as enallage/continued single speaker across a person shift, or accept the cut - rather than by denying the marker. Any bound change is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption. Regardless of where the bound lands, add the cross-seam disclosure required by the byte-true device at the row's back seam (see the escalated ruling on this row). Cure test (the test that killed the original): a word-final-kaf audit over MT 6:4-6:9 must not contradict any absence wording left anywhere on the row, and no unsupported universal may remain.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL's DISTINCT sub-claim on the same row: an undisclosed byte-identical inclusio straddles the row's back seam, arguing the praise frame closes at 6:10 rather than at 6:9.
rulings.grounds: The bytes are verified and the disclosure defect is real: אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת closes oshb:Song.6.4 and closes oshb:Song.6.10 byte-identically (byte sweep: 2 verses book-wide), and בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא (oshb:Song.6.9) / בָּרָה֙ (oshb:Song.6.10) cross the same seam - a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam, undisclosed, which the cross-seam cohesion rule says argues continuity against the row. What is NOT an ordinary defect call is the boundary consequence, and it is genuinely contested at owner level. On one side: the 6:9|6:10 join carries no tier-1 voice-shift marker at all (zero 2fs forms in either verse; see the companion ruling), so the hybrid rule's 'refrain verses close units' clause plus this byte-tier inclusio would make WEB 6:10 the closing member of the unit opened at 6:4 and would dissolve the standalone single-verse row at WEB 6:10. On the other side: the mi-zot formula anchor functions as a movement OPENER at both of its other attested sites - מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier) opening the litter procession, and the same run opening oshb:Song.8.5 (byte sweep of that run: 2 verses) - which argues WEB 6:10 opens rather than closes. The closed vocabulary and the granularity rule set no precedence between an attested refrain-formula anchor and an ad-hoc byte-identical inclusio meeting at one verse, and the tier-3 SAMEKH sited at both MT 6:9 and MT 6:10 (single-witness, never a driver) cannot break the tie in either direction. Escalated as a refrain-bracket vs unit-frame precedence question governing this row's back seam and the very existence of the WEB 6:10 row.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF and OL raise the SAME core defect - 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' fails on the front edge, since MT 6:9 and MT 6:10 are alike third-person feminine predication. OL adds two DISTINCT defects: the three-site recurrence is carried at a tier the row never names, and the 'ascending' label imports an element absent from the verse's own bytes.
rulings.grounds: All three sustained on re-derivation. FRONT SEAM (same defect in both packets): the word-final-kaf audit finds zero 2fs forms in EITHER MT 6:9 or MT 6:10; MT 6:9 predicates הִיא֙ three times with the 3fs mappiq suffixes לְאִמָּ֔הּ / לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier), and MT 6:10 continues feminine-singular predication with הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier). The last actual 2fs address in the neighbourhood is לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier), three verses earlier; the יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י epithets at MT 6:9 are 1cs-possessive, addressive in flavour but not address forms. The row's bilateral claim therefore holds on the BACK side only, where the 3fs-to-1cs shift into יָרַ֔דְתִּי (oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) is real and correctly grounds that edge. What the front edge does carry is weaker and different from what the row asserts: the speaker's 1cs possessive epithets drop out after MT 6:9 and the form turns declarative-to-interrogative. TIER DEFECT (OL, distinct, upheld): the row's own מִי זֹ֥את (oshb:Song.6.10) is byte tier at 1 verse; the three-site count is an accent_stripped/skeleton object (sweep: 3 verses at both tiers - MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5), and no tier is named, against the tier-disclosure standard that a skeleton-tier cohesion driver meets the byte-grounded bar ONLY with the tier honestly named. LABEL DEFECT (OL, distinct, upheld): 'ascending-question' imports a byte-absent element - the ascending verb is attested in מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier) and at MT 8:5 (word-bound skeleton sweep of that verb: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5) and is ABSENT from MT 6:10, whose participle is הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה. OL's high severity is sustained rather than reduced: this is a single-verse row whose independent existence rests entirely on the front cut, and tier-3 SAMEKH corroboration cannot carry a boundary whose tier-1 evidence does not survive.
rulings.remedy: Strike 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' from boundary_rationale. If the row survives the escalated boundary question, state the front-edge signals in their true terms - loss of the speaker's 1cs possessive epithets after MT 6:9, the declarative-to-interrogative form change, and the mi-zot formula anchor - and tier-label that recurrence as accent_stripped/skeleton (sweep: 3 verses), replacing 'ascending-question' with a label MT 6:10's own bytes carry (the participial who-is-this-who-looks-out class). Re-cut observed_substrate_signals to the surviving driver, and re-open rejected_alternative and confidence with it. Cure tests (the tests that killed the original): a word-final-kaf plus 1cs/3fs audit over MT 6:9-6:10 must not contradict any person-shift wording left on the row; every recurrence sentence must name its tier; and no element of a formula label may be asserted that a sweep of the row's own verse cannot find.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row never argues its own front boundary: neither the rationale nor boundary_evidence_refs addresses why the row does not continue 6:12's voice, despite an available tier-1 warrant.
rulings.grounds: Verified against the row and the bytes. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative address only the verse's internal two-voice structure and the BACK seam; MT 6:12 appears nowhere on the row, and the refs-mirror check returns GREEN precisely because no out-of-span mention of 6:12 exists to mirror - the silence is total, not a citation slip. The unused tier-1 warrant is real: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in first person singular (לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי, נַפְשִׁ֣י, שָׂמַ֔תְנִי, oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) and oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens with a repeated 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (byte tier) addressed to an epithet unique to this verse (הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית; byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse) - an addressee-and-person shift of exactly the tier-1 class. One collateral assertion in the LF item is itself byte-false and is NOT adopted: the row's offset-zone dual-cite discipline is not followed throughout (see the OL ruling on this row); the front-boundary finding survives that correction.
rulings.remedy: Add the front-seam argument to boundary_rationale with both forms spliced and tier-labelled - the 1cs run at oshb:Song.6.12 against the 2fs imperative summons and the הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית epithet at oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 - and add web:Song.6.12 to boundary_evidence_refs. In the same edit disclose the catchword that crosses this seam: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after, skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide, bracketing the single-verse span on both seams. Cure test: every verse argued in prose outside the row's own span appears in boundary_evidence_refs and the refs-mirror check stays GREEN after the addition; the front seam must be defensible from an in-verse marker, never from the WEB voice heading.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row states that every structured ref on it carries the dual-cite qualifier and that is false - its rejected-alternative sentence carries a bare offset-zone coordinate - and it argues its own held voice crux without quoting the verse's decisive plural form.
rulings.grounds: Both halves verified, including OL's account of why no machine flag fires - DISTINCT from the LF item on this row, which concerns the unargued front seam. strongest_rejected_alternative writes the structured coordinate 'web:Song.7.1' (i.e. web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2) bare on the row - no dual, no numeric qualifier - while device_notes asserts that every structured ref on the row carries the dual-cite qualifier. In this book that bare coordinate resolves to oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, and standing in a sentence about extending the row FORWARD it is readable as the row's own verse (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1) - the exact ambiguity the offset-zone rule exists to prevent. Machine state confirms the rule-level character of the leak: the citation sweep returns GREEN for these rows because its offset-zone disclosure arm iterates the boundary_evidence_refs list only (confirmed at source), so a bare offset-zone coordinate sitting in a prose field is not covered; the universals check independently flags 'every structured ref on it carries the dual-cite qualifier' as a digit-less universal, and it is false on the row's own text. Engagement gap verified: the row quotes the summons and תֶּחֱזוּ֙ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) but omits the form between them - וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a 1cp cohortative with a 2fs suffix - which is the in-verse byte evidence that the summoners are plural and the addressee feminine, exactly the question the row holds open.
rulings.remedy: Qualify the coordinate in strongest_rejected_alternative as 'web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2' (or 'web:Song.7.1 (MT 7:2)'), and either delete the device_notes universal or restate it as a checked claim. Splice וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) into the crux sentence, tier-labelled, as the plural-speaker evidence being weighed against the 2mp תֶּחֱזוּ֙ - the crux stays HELD, not decided. Cure test (the test that killed the original is prose-side, not machine-side): a hand sweep of EVERY structured coordinate in EVERY field, not only boundary_evidence_refs, must show a dual or numeric qualifier on each, since the deterministic arm does not reach prose fields; and no unsupported universal may remain on the row.

supported_sample.claim_checked: device_notes: the row closes on one of the six banot-yerushalaim adjacent-pair ADDRESS sites (sweep: 6 verses), a distinct object from the bare banot count.
supported_sample.notes: A word-bound adjacent-pair sweep returns exactly 6 verses (MT 1:5, 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 5:16, 8:4); an unbound substring sweep returns 7 by catching the from-phrase מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier) at MT 3:10 - which is precisely the address-vs-phrase hazard the object-discipline rule exists for, and the row's object and its digit are both right. The closing tokens of the row's last verse are בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Song.5.16, byte tier). The span maps to the same MT verses through the crosswalk (checked, not assumed), so its bare coordinates are legitimate, and no parashah seg falls in the span or on either seam, so the row's silence on the tier-3 layer is correct rather than a symmetry gap.

supported_sample.claim_checked: boundary_rationale: no tier-1 marker separates 6:11 from 6:12 - the same first-person-singular voice runs through both.
supported_sample.notes: First-person forms in both verses (יָרַ֔דְתִּי at oshb:Song.6.11; לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי, נַפְשִׁ֣י, שָׂמַ֔תְנִי at oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier); the surface audit finds zero word-final-kaf 2fs tokens and zero 3fs mappiq suffixes in either verse, so nothing of the tier-1 class competes at the internal join the row declines to cut. No parashah seg falls at that join (the single-witness inventory carries none at MT 6:11) and the SAMEKH the row cites at MT 6:10 does match the inventory. WEB 6:11 and WEB 6:12 map to the same MT verses through the crosswalk, i.e. the span sits immediately BEFORE the offset zone, so the bare coordinates are legitimate. One undisclosed residual confirmed, not contesting these bounds: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12) recurs as בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1) - skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide - crossing the row's back seam.
